$comment: #255 / #381 — known input-plugin metadata gaps (#381 added epaRegistrationNumber for herbicides, insecticides and fungicides). Every entry needs a reason. The coverage test fails on any gap not listed here AND on any entry that is no longer a gap, so remove entries as plugins are label-verified.

entries.reason: Generic 2,4-D amine plugin with no brand or EPA number. Amine jugs from different registrants differ in salt, strength and label wording, so the formulation code has to come from the jug on hand (rechecked 2026-10-04).
Generic 2,4-D plugin with no brand or EPA number. Dozens of 2,4-D registrations (amine salts, esters, choline) differ in formulation, so no one label's code applies (rechecked 2026-10-04).

Labels (62719-597, 2024 and 2011, plus Greenbook specimen), the Corteva 2019 fact sheet and the Dow SDS (v5.1, 2016, section 9 'Physical state Granules') name no formulation type. Only PPLS ('Water Dispersible Granule') and retailer blurbs say WDG. Rechecked 2026-10-04.
Generic FIFRA 25(b) material with no brand: corn gluten meal is sold as meal, powder, granules or pellets by many marketers, so no single label or tech sheet names its form (rechecked 2026-10-04).

Crossbow label (62719-260, 2025-02-04) prints no formulation code or name, and no Corteva tech sheet, SDS line or product page naming one was found (the corteva.com Crossbow page is gone). PPLS 'Emulsifiable Concentrate' is corroboration only. Rechecked 2026-10-04.
E2E clickthrough test fixture, not a real product: no label exists, so no formulation code applies.

Generic 'Glyphosate 41%' with no brand or EPA number. Most 41% IPA-salt jugs are soluble liquids, but that is not printed for any one product, so the code must come from the jug's label (rechecked 2026-10-04).

GrazonNext HL master label (62719-628, 2017) and the Corteva 2019 fact sheet print no formulation code or wording, and the product page has none. PPLS says Emulsifiable Concentrate, which is doubtful for two amine salts. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Halex GT labels (100-1282, 2025 and 2008), the Syngenta SDS (2023-05-30, only 'Appearance: liquid') and the DoseLock info sheet print no formulation type or code, only 'DoseLock Formulation Technology'. PPLS 'Emulsifiable Concentrate' is corroboration only. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Liberty ULTRA label (7969-500, 2025 and 2024) says only it 'is a water-soluble nonselective herbicide'; the BASF SDS (v2.0, 2024-10-29) gives 'Form: liquid' and 'completely soluble'. No BASF document prints soluble liquid/SL. PPLS formulations field is empty. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

FIFRA 25(b) product with no EPA label. The manufacturer label calls it only a liquid 'herbicide CONCENTRATE' and the Soil Technologies SDS (2017-02-23) gives only 'Physical State: Liquid'; neither names a formulation type. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Label (62719-756, 2025) and the Corteva tech bulletin (020567 COR 09/24) call it only 'encapsulated' (encapsulated acetochlor in a premix with mesotrione and clopyralid), so CS vs ZC cannot be settled. Trade press says ZC (not a registrant source). PPLS formulation field is empty.

Stinger labels (62719-73, 2019 and 2014) and the corteva.com product page print no formulation code or type; the label states only clopyralid MEA salt 40.9% (3 lb ae/gal). PPLS says 'Emulsifiable Concentrate', doubtful for an amine salt. Rechecked 2026-10-04.
Generic Btk active-ingredient plugin with no label rate: the unit (lb for DF/WG, fl oz for liquids) depends on which Bt product is bought, so none can be set (rechecked 2026-10-04).

Generic Btk active-ingredient plugin with no brand or rate: registered Btk products are DF, WG, WP, liquid and dust (Javelin WG, DiPel DF), so no single code applies. Use the brand plugins (dipel-df, javelin-wg).

Hand-applied pheromone twist-tie dispenser (PPLS 'Impregnated Materials'). The enum only has spray, granule and dust codes, each mapped to liquid or dry, and neither fits a dispenser. Formulation only feeds the liquid/dry default-unit derivation, and the plugin already sets defaultUnit 'count', so no schema change is proposed.

Label 65564-1 prints only 'spray emulsion'; the JMS Flower Farms Organic Stylet-Oil SDS (2002) says 'paraffinic oil plus non-ionic emulsification system', not a formulation type. 'Emulsifiable concentrate' appears only in a New Zealand SDS issued by Etec Crop Solutions (NZ registration, 2017).

Label 65564-1 (2011) prints only 'dilute spray emulsion'; the JMS Flower Farms SDS (1994) says 'paraffinic distillate plus non-ionic emulsification system', not a formulation type. 'Emulsifiable concentrate' appears only in a New Zealand SDS issued by Etec Crop Solutions (NZ registration). PPLS type 'Oils (no added pesticide)'.

M-Pede label (10163-324, 2021) says only 'The formulation is based on potassium salts of naturally derived fatty acids'; the Gowan SDS (2012-01-12) gives only 'Appearance: Yellow liquid'. PPLS 'Soluble Concentrate' is corroboration only. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Madex HP label (69553-1, 2026) prints no formulation and PPLS says 'Ready-to-Use Solution', which conflicts with dilution use. 'SC' appears only as the test substance in the Certis SDS ecotox table and on Andermatt's sheet for the sibling brand Madex, not for Madex HP. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Live beneficial nematodes sold as infective juveniles in sachets or carrier (e.g. Koppert Entonem, 50 or 250 million). No enum code (all mapped to liquid or dry) describes a live organism. Formulation only feeds the default-unit derivation and defaultUnit 'count' is set, so no schema change is proposed.
Generic spinosad active-ingredient plugin with no ratePerAcre: the unit (fl oz for SC, oz for WP) depends on which product is bought, so none can be set (rechecked 2026-10-04).
Generic spinosad active-ingredient plugin with no brand or rate: spinosad is sold as SC (Entrust SC, Success) and WP (Entrust 80W), so no single code applies.

Live parasitoid release sold as parasitized-egg cards or cups (e.g. TRICHOforce B). No enum code (all mapped to liquid or dry) describes a live insect release. Formulation only feeds the default-unit derivation and defaultUnit 'count' is set, so no schema change is proposed.

Venerate XC is an alternate brand of MBI-206 EP (EPA 84059-14); its label names no standard code ('EP' is not one). The only printed SC on 84059-14 is the trade-name synonym 'MBI-305 EP, Majestene SC' in the ProFarm SDS (MBI-SDS-0009 rev 10, 2023), which is likely a non-US trade name (rev 9's note says 'Update synonyms', and the French/African distributor Elephant Vert sells a MAJESTENE SC); the US master label (MBI-206 EP, 2026-02-02) lists MAJESTENE and VENERATE brands side by side and never mentions MBI-305 or SC. PPLS says Emulsifiable Concentrate. Majestene and Venerate XC are one US product and stay gapped together (panel ruling 2026-10-04, #553, 3-0).

Voliam Xpress label (100-1320, 2025) says only 'an aqueous based formulation'; the Syngenta SDS (2015-06-30) gives only 'Light beige to brown liquid'. Sister Besiege is a Zeon Concentrate (CS + SC), which is unprinted for Voliam. PPLS says EC. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

Mycoshield label (55146-97, 2019 master and 2007) prints no formulation words; the Nufarm SDS (2018-03-26) says only 'Light to dark brown powder', which fits WP or SP. Only PPLS (WP) and a USDA AMS report say wettable powder. Rechecked 2026-10-04.

ProPhyt master label (42519-22, 2025) prints no formulation words; the Helena SDS (2019-11-05) says 'Transparent blue liquid' and the product page only 'Easy-to-use liquid' (marketing, no Formulation field). PPLS 'Soluble Concentrate' is corroboration only. Rechecked 2026-10-04.
Generic plugin: '2,4-D Amine' names an active ingredient, not one registrant's product; dozens of EPA registrations exist and the number depends on the jug on hand (checked 2026-09-25).
Generic plugin: PPLS lists many active "2,4-D Amine" registrations (e.g. 87290-45, 33270-21, 93930-42, 1381-103, 62719-2), so the number depends on the jug on hand.
Generic plugin: PPLS lists many active "Atrazine 4L" registrations (e.g. 33270-10, 2749-657, 94730-23, 35915-4, 5905-470), so the number depends on the jug on hand.
Generic plugin: PPLS lists many active clethodim 2EC registrations (e.g. 228-735, 38167-39, 87290-11, 92647-31, 34704-864), so the number depends on the jug on hand.

Generic: PPLS search 'Clethodim 2EC'/'Clethodim 2E' (2026-09-25) returns 12+ active registrations from different registrants (e.g. 38167-39, 87290-11, 93809-5, 34704-864, 70506-481, 228-735); number depends on the jug on hand.
Generic plugin: 'Clethodim 2EC' names an active ingredient and concentration sold by many registrants; the EPA number depends on the jug on hand (checked 2026-09-25).

Exempt/generic: corn gluten meal is a FIFRA 25(b) minimum-risk active; PPLS search 'Corn Gluten' (2026-09-25) returns no registrations. Plugin names no single marketed product, so there is no number to record.
E2E clickthrough test fixture, not a real product; no EPA registration exists or should be assigned.

Generic: PPLS search 'Glyphosate 41' (2026-09-25) returns many active registrations from different registrants (e.g. 5905-635, 87659-3, 84229-36, 85945-1, 88343-4, 71995-7, 103822-3); number depends on the jug on hand.

Generic: PPLS search 'Mesotrione 4SC' (2026-09-25) returns 10+ active registrations from different registrants (e.g. 89168-54, 93809-1, 84229-48, 42750-315, 93182-30, 87290-61, 60063-66); number depends on the jug on hand.

Plugin spans two brands with two registrants and stays one plugin (#530: not split). Checked PPLS 2026-10-03: Treflan HFP is 10163-363 (Gowan, Active; transferred from Corteva 62719-250 on 2016-08-15; newest label 2026-06-23), while Trust is WinField 1381-146 ('TRUST HERBICIDE', label 2015-05-26) or 1381-261 ('TRUST', label 2024-07-17), and neither Trust label says HFP. No single number fits 'Treflan / Trust HFP'; use the number on the jug on hand.

Generic active-ingredient entry, not one registrant's product: PPLS lists many active Btk registrations (e.g. 34 active DiPel records, Javelin 70051-60/70051-66), and DiPel DF and Javelin WG have their own plugins. Checked 2026-09-25.
Live entomopathogenic nematodes are macro-organisms, exempt from FIFRA registration under 40 CFR 152.20(a). No EPA number exists (producer page for Koppert Entonem shows no EPA reg. no.).

Generic entry: 'Spinosad' names an active ingredient, not one registrant's product. PPLS lists many spinosad products (Entrust, Success, Monterey etc.), each with its own number. The number depends on the product on hand.

Generic product: plugin names no registrant. PPLS lists many active wettable sulfurs (e.g. Drexel Sulfur 90W 19713-238, Yellow Jacket 6325-13, Clean Crop 6325-13-34704); the number depends on the bag on hand. Checked 2026-09-25.

Trichogramma egg parasitoids are macro-organisms (beneficial insects), exempt from FIFRA registration under 40 CFR 152.20(a). The producer page (Beneficial Insectary TRICHOforce B) shows no EPA number.
FIFRA 25(b) minimum-risk product (Soil Technologies Corp. label, OMRI 10/2022): 'This product has not been registered by the U.S. E.P.A.' No EPA Reg. No. exists; 82557-3 is Sinon Methomyl 90 WSP.
FIFRA 25(b) minimum-risk product (JH Biotech Weed Zap label: 'exempt from registration ... under section 25 (b) of FIFRA'). No EPA Reg. No.; 84718-1 does not exist in PPLS.

Generic plugin: several active dimethoate 4EC registrations (Loveland 34704-207, Drexel 19713-231, UPL 70506-453, FMC 279-3541); the number depends on the jug on hand. The previous 5905-368 was Omni Supreme Spray (a mineral oil). Rechecked 2026-10-03 (#530): the plugin notes say Loveland Products, but Loveland's 34704-207 is titled 'DIMETHOATE 400' on PPLS and on every label file (2007-2014), never 'Dimethoate 4EC', so it is not taken as the plugin's product.

Majestene is an alternate brand of MBI-206 EP (EPA 84059-14), whose 2026-02-02 master label prints no formulation code or type (SDS section 9: 'PHYSICAL STATE: Liquid'). The only printed SC on 84059-14 is the trade-name synonym 'MBI-305 EP, Majestene SC' in the ProFarm SDS (MBI-SDS-0009 rev 10, 2023), which is likely a non-US trade name (rev 9's note says 'Update synonyms', and the French/African distributor Elephant Vert sells a MAJESTENE SC); the US master label (MBI-206 EP, 2026-02-02) lists MAJESTENE and VENERATE brands side by side and never mentions MBI-305 or SC. PPLS says Emulsifiable Concentrate. Majestene and Venerate XC are one US product and stay gapped together (panel ruling 2026-10-04, #553, 3-0).

Both labels in PPLS (055146-00057-20030127 and -20220727) say only 'Champ Dry Prill', and Nufarm's bulletin says 'FORMULATION dry prill' (not a code); the Nufarm SDS (2015) gives only 'Teal blue granular solid', 'Dispersible'. The only 'Dry Flowable' is the 2003 EPA Form 8570-1 product name 'Nufarm Champion Formula 2 Dry Flowable Fungicide', an application form, not a label, tech sheet or SDS, so the #554 DF fill was reverted (panel ruling 2026-10-04, #553, 2-1). PPLS says Water Dispersible Granule. Dry product either way, matching the lb rate.

FIFRA 25(b) product with no EPA label; the JH Biotech label calls it only 'WEED ZAP concentrate'. JH's flyer ('WeedZap Info 1-1-20') and SDS say only 'Form: Liquid' / 'Physical state liquid', a physical state like the refused liberty-ultra and m-pede evidence, so the #554 L fill was reverted (panel ruling 2026-10-04, #553, 3-0: L only when a registrant document says 'liquid formulation' or has a 'Formulation: liquid' field).
